source_policy: Primary references support definitions and stated conditions. Scenarios and worked derivations are originally authored constructions. The supplied book matrix guides sequencing; it is not independent verification of exact-edition book coverage.
purpose: Follow a binary library counter through a writable tape, a moving head and the exact carry that adds one.
meaning: A Turing machine combines finite control with a writable tape and a read-write head. Its configuration includes the current state, head position and tape contents. This original binary-increment program scans to the word’s right edge, carries left, then halts; its intermediate tape reading is not yet the increment result.

definition.setting: A deterministic binary-increment machine with a two-sided tape, four selectable four-bit words and a finite view of exact whole transitions.

signature.qₖ: Current finite control state after the selected transitions, stopping at halt.
signature.hₖ: Current head address on the integer-addressed tape.
signature.vₖ: Unsigned value of the current written binary numeral; intermediate until halt.
signature.δ: Transition function assigning next state, written symbol and head direction.
signature.□: Blank tape symbol, distinct from the digit 0.
signature.L: Move the tape head one address left.
signature.R: Move the tape head one address right.

conditions: The input alphabet consists of the two digits 0 and 1. The selected input word w is one of 0101, 1011, 1111 or 0000. Its four bits occupy integer tape addresses 0 through 3; all other cells are blank □. The head begins at address 0 in state S.

The writable tape extends in both directions. The read/write head selects one tape cell; a tape read obtains its current symbol. Each machine step reads that cell, writes one symbol, follows the head direction left or right, and changes the finite control state according to the transition rule. The finite viewport contains every visited cell for the four available inputs.

State S scans right without altering bits. On the first blank to the right, it enters carry state C and moves left. In C, a 1 becomes 0 and the head moves left; a 0 or blank becomes 1 and the machine enters H after moving right.
H is a halting state with no outgoing transition. Scrubbing beyond the actual halt leaves the configuration and actual transition count unchanged.

The displayed unsigned tape numeral vₖ can decrease while the carry is propagating. It equals the completed input-plus-one result only after the machine halts. Leading zeros remain visible; overflow can write one bit to the left of the original word.
definition.domain_notes: This is one explicitly stated Turing-machine variant and one small program. The display covers its selected inputs, not every tape configuration. It does not establish universality, the Church–Turing thesis or undecidability.
definition.proof_status: Definition-level sources and original restricted-family arguments; independent review pending.

grammar.formation_rule: Start with w at addresses 0 through 3, state S and head address 0. Apply the stated read-write-move transition table at most k times, stopping immediately at H. Read the current unsigned binary numeral from the written tape; call it the completed increment result only if H has been reached.

properties.claim: The program increments each available input word by one.
properties.conditions: Use the stated scanning and carry transition table.
properties.derivation: Scanning leaves the word unchanged. In carry state, a trailing block of 1s becomes zeros; the first preceding 0 becomes 1, or a new leading 1 is written on a blank. This is binary addition of one.

properties.claim: The finite state alone does not determine the configuration.
properties.conditions: A configuration includes state, head address and tape contents.
properties.derivation: Carry state C can occur with different head positions and different partially rewritten tape words; those differences determine subsequent reads.

prompts.prompt: Can the current tape value decrease during a correct increment?
prompts.answer: Yes. Changing a trailing 1 to 0 lowers that intermediate reading while the carry continues left. The final increment is read only at halt.

prompts.prompt: Does the head remain on the last bit written?
prompts.answer: Not in this convention. Each transition also moves left or right; the transition into H moves right after writing.
